- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.
- After a price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust downward slightly in 2nd–3rd period.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates in early periods when sentiment is rising; add 0.5–1.5% to first 3–5 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.00 or 0.33), model tends to ignore downward momentum; increase downward bias in forecast.
- If sentiment is high and price is near 78+, model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 78–79 unless sentiment confirms breakout.
